for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 420 R/W 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text:
It is stated that a petition was filed under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking dissolution of the marriage on mutual consent, in M.C.No.7911/2024 before the Principal Judge,
Family Court at Bengaluru and the Court has granted a decree of divorce on 13.01.2025 as per the terms of the settlement entered between the parties.

entities.text:
Principal Judge,

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Further, as per the memorandum of settlement,
petitioner has to pay a sum of  7,00,000/- to respondent No. 2 towards her maintenance,
education and other expenses of the minor child, on or before 31.12.2025.
4. The petitioner and respondent No.2 are present before the Court, they are identified by their respective learned counsel.

5. Petitioner has handed over a Demand Draft bearing No.491006 dated 01.12.2025 drawn on Canara Bank, NC: 2025:KHC:49937 HC-KAR Uttarahally Branch, Bengaluru, in the name of second respondent, for a sum of  7,00,000./-.
6.
The receipt of the Demand Draft has been acknowledged by the second respondent and the learned counsel appearing for the said respondent.

7. Matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute, wherein the parties have settled the dispute and by virtue of the mutual consent petition filed before the Family Court, Bengaluru, the marriage between petitioner and respondent No.2 has been dissolved.
In terms of the settlement, petitioner has paid a sum of  7,00,000/- to respondent No.2.

8. Respondent No.2/defacto complainant present before the Court and submits that in view of the settlement, she is not interested in proceeding with the case any further and she has no objection to quash the entire proceedings now pending before the trial Court.
9. In this case, FIR is registered against the petitioner and two others i.e. petitioner and in-laws of respondent No.2.
On completion of investigation charge sheet has been filed.
In view of the compromise between the parties and the joint affidavit filed, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the criminal proceedings pending against all the accused.
Hence, in the interest of justice, it is desirable to quash the entire proceedings.
Accordingly, the following ORDER IA No.2/2025 is allowed.
Consequently, petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings arising out of Crime No.271/2021 of Subramanyapura Police Station,
pending before the 30th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru, in C.C.No. 31198/2022,
as against accused No.1 to 3, for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 420 r/w 34 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are quashed.
IA No.1/2025 is disposed of.
